text:
Tara: FYI Silverpine is asking to lock dedicated capacity for Q3. They requested 45 A100-80GB GPUs reserved, and mentioned they expect sustained utilization (models in-prod) ~100% during business hours. They asked for a 20% "safety band" + monthly burst credits. Can we run the sizing and a counter-proposal?
Mike: quick question — the ask says A100-80GB, right? not 40GB?
Tara: yes A100-80GB. Customer explicitly called out large context models and reranking pipelines.
Arjun: conservative approach: use 1.15 safety multiplier for production spikes + explicit burst credits. 20% seems high unless they have big periodic training runs. Suggest 15% safety + 10% burst credits.
Priya: from sales perspective they'd prefer the 20% if it reduces throttling risk, but we can trade off price for lower headroom. Thinking: commit + 15% band + 10% burst credits with a 10% committed discount.
Jess: note: eu-west-1 currently has some AZ-level capacity constraints in late-week windows. If we provision all 45 in a single AZ we might hit placement failures during peakhours. Recommend multi-AZ spread and pre-warm pool.
ops-bot: capacity-check: eu-west-1 available free A100-80GB capacity: 320 GPUs across AZs, but only ~70 GPUs immediate warm in az-1 (can cold-start additional in ~90-120m).
Lukas: proposed config snippet (for sizing docs):
```
committed_gpus: 45
safety_multiplier: 1.15
provisioned_gpus: 52  # ceil(45 * 1.15)
burst_credit_pct: 0.10  # fraction of monthly commit usable as bursts
prewarm_pool: 2_per_az
placement: multi-az
SLA_prewarm: 4h
```
Tara: can you translate that to GPU-hours/day and monthly GPU-hours so sales can include numbers in the term sheet?
Mike: math: committed_gpus * 24 = 45 * 24 = 1080 GPU-hrs/day. With safety 1.15 -> provisioned 52 GPUs -> 52 * 24 = 1248 GPU-hrs/day. Burst credits 10% of monthly commit -> monthly commit = 1080 * 30 = 32,400 GPU-hrs/month -> 10% burst = 3,240 GPU-hrs/month (~108 GPU-hrs/day equivalent if used evenly).
Jess: important to call out: burst credits are not pre-provisioned capacity; they are credits that allow ephemeral overage subject to capacity availability and may cold-start. We'll guarantee pre-warm for 4h SLA only for the committed band + prewarm pool.
Priya: pricing draft: committed band (45 gpus) @ committed-rate X, safety provision (7 GPUs) billed as part of reserved capacity but at lower discount tier? OR we can bill committed baseline and include safety as part of reservation (preferred by customers). Recommend bundling safety into reserved capacity to avoid surprise overage charges. Offer 10% discount across the whole committed+band bundle.
Arjun: ops notes — to implement: (1) mark 45 GPUs as "hard-commit", (2) mark 7 GPUs as "soft-buffer" with autoscale policy to allow consumption before dipping into burst credits, (3) prewarm 2 GPUs per AZ for p99 latency protection on scale-up. Also add routing policy to route to alternate region on local capacity shortages.
Tara: action items: Arjun to produce sizing doc + autoscale policy snippet, Lukas to confirm multi-AZ placement feasibility and cold-start timings, Jess to write a short note about SLOs for burst behavior, Priya to draft term sheet with the numbers and 10% discount. I'll consolidate and send to Silverpine by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Mike: I'll run a quick sim against our Q3 demand curve to validate 1.15 vs 1.2 numbers and post results here.
Priya: if the sim shows frequent >15% spikes during their local business hours, we'll circle back and propose a small extra buffer or higher burst allotment.
Tara: thanks — feel free to drop short notes here with updates.
